verified_reason: Lamontagne-Lacasse 2011: RCT, CrM vs placebo for 28 d in 12 elite university volleyball players (8 analysed). Abstract reports spike-jump and repeated block-jump height only and says nothing about the training programme, body mass or adverse events. No open full text in Europe PMC, so only the full text can decide; expect E03 or E05 unless a structured RT programme and body-mass/strength data are reported

Claudino 2014: resolved from open full text (PMC4077550). RCT, CrM (20 g/d for 1 wk, then 5 g/d for 6 wk) vs dextrose placebo during a 7-wk pre-season in 14 professional soccer players aged 18.3 +/- 0.9 y. Both arms did the same supervised, hypertrophy-oriented RT twice a week (squat, bench press, lat pull-down, leg press, shoulder press, 3 x 8-10RM) plus plyometrics and soccer training. Eligible outcome is body mass only (secondary); countermovement jump is not a protocol outcome. Age range not reported, mean 18.3 y: confirm at full-text eligibility

E02: Simpson 2019, resolved from open full text (PMC6693921). Youth elite soccer players aged 16-21 y, mean 17.4 +/- 1.6 y (13 under-18 and 6 under-21 players), so the sample is mainly 16-17 y. Also little RT (about one 50-min strength and conditioning session per week). Adverse-event context only: one creatine player reported minor GI discomfort; unfavourable airway trends (FENO, FEV1 fall) did not reach significance

Fernandez-Landa 2020 (Biomolecules): the abstract supports the exclusion, but the open full text (PMC7022312) does not. RCT, CrM 0.04 g/kg/d vs placebo (plus HMB and CrM+HMB arms) for 10 wk in 28 elite male rowers aged 30.4 +/- 4.7 y; all arms did identical training, 6 x 1.5 h/wk, of which 30% was resistance training in a gym. Table 2 reports body mass and skinfold/girth-derived muscle-mass and fat-mass percentages by group (no group x time interaction). So an RT component and an eligible secondary outcome exist. Decide at full-text eligibility whether a 30% gym share with no stated prescription counts as a structured RT programme. Same trial as SP1-0698 (excluded E03 in batch 004 on its abstract), which must be reopened with it; one of the two would become E08. This overturn triggers the rescue rule

E03: Lifanov 2014, short-term creatine vs dextrose in 21 football players analysed by AMPD1/PPARG genotype; no duration or RT programme stated, VO2max and blood lactate only. No open full text; nothing in the abstract points to an eligible outcome

E03: Elstad 2023, protein + carbohydrate with vs without 5 g creatine for 21-26 d in 30 firefighters; occupational task times only. Open full text (PMC10745745) confirms no training programme was imposed and the intervention is under 4 wk (E07 also applies)

E03: Moesgaard 2024, creatine vs placebo loading + maintenance in endurance-trained adults, then acute caffeine/bicarbonate crossover trials; open full text shows no RT programme; MVC, 15-s sprint and 6-min time trial are acute test outcomes

E03: Graef 2009, creatine citrate vs placebo with 4 wk of cycling HIIT only; no RT programme (full text has no resistance training); VO2peak and ventilatory threshold outcomes. Consistent with SP1-0548
E04: morning vs evening creatine intake for 12 wk in 14 female handball players; creatine in both arms. Open full text confirms there was no creatine-free control group
E02: Yanez-Silva 2017, youth soccer players mean age 17.0 +/- 0.5 y; also only 14 days of creatine (E07) with Wingate outcomes
E07: single acute dose of a multi-ingredient pre-exercise supplement (caffeine, creatine, amino acids) vs placebo, treadmill runs; E14 would also apply

da Silveira 2014: downgraded from include after reading the open full text (PMC4332172). In favour: double-blind RCT, creatine (0.3 g/kg/d for 1 wk, then 0.03 g/kg/d) vs glutamine vs cornflour placebo for 93 days, 32 healthy male military police officers aged 18-30, same supervised training in all arms. Against: the training is general Military Physical Training, 5 x 90 min/wk, described only as a mix of neuromuscular and cardiopulmonary exercise with no RT prescription (no exercises, loads, sets or progression), and the authors themselves say the activities were not standardised. Outcomes are push-ups, sit-ups, horizontal jump, shuttle run and Cooper test: no 1RM, body mass, body composition, renal marker or adverse-event data. Push-up count is the only candidate (muscular endurance, secondary). Leans E03 at full-text eligibility; kept as maybe because the call depends on how the protocol defines a structured RT programme, which should be settled once for this record, SP7-0097 and SP8-0219 together

SR/MA mapping: Marinho 2023, systematic review (8 databases, QualSyst appraisal, 10 studies) of creatine + caffeine co-ingestion. A creatine plus co-ingredient review counts as creatine-specific under the 10:29 rule. The source trials include creatine-alone and placebo arms, and nothing in the abstract excludes an RT co-intervention, so it passes on the intervention, comparator and design parts. Caveat: all 10 included studies are 3-6 day loading designs, so the citation-chasing yield for our PICOS is probably nil. Full text is not open; recode E05 if its criteria restrict to loading-only or acute protocols (same handling as SP6-0003)

SR/MA mapping: Metzger 2023, creatine-specific review run to PRISMA (PubMed and EMBASE, 9,393 records screened against pre-defined criteria, 13 studies, 268 participants). Its restriction to healthy paediatric/adolescent athletes is a population criterion, which does not count under the rule as clarified at 12:28 (same handling as SP6-0020). Intervention, comparator and design parts pass: more than 75% of its studies are RCTs of creatine and RT is not excluded. Low yield expected (mean ages 11.5-18.2 y, mostly soccer and swimming), and the trials it yields will mostly be E02 for us

SR/MA mapping: Pinto 2016, creatine-specific systematic review (PubMed type Systematic Review) of creatine with or without exercise training and glucose metabolism. It covers human placebo-controlled trials of creatine with exercise training, so it can admit a trial meeting our PICOS; outcomes do not count under the rule, and the animal studies it also includes do not disqualify it. Weak review: the abstract gives no databases, counts or appraisal method
